Class CharWriter

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.io.CharWriter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, Flushable, Appendable, AutoCloseable
public final class CharWriter extends Object implements Appendable, Closeable, Flushable
Writes a stream of characters, with calls that chain.

A writer on a Writer holds a buffer, which it writes to the stream when it is full, on flush() and on close(). A writer on any other Appendable, such as a StringBuilder, writes to it directly. 

try (var out = CharSink.of(file).openWriter()) {
    out.write("# ").writeLine(title);
    for (var entry : entries) {
        out.write(entry.key()).write(" = ").writeLine(entry.value());
    }
}

A writer owns its stream: close() closes it, and any write after that throws IOException. A writer is not safe for use by several threads at once.

Since:
0.2.0

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static CharWriter of(Writer out)
      Returns a writer that writes to a stream, which it then owns. If out is the stream view of a writer, returns that writer rather than buffering its characters again.
      Parameters:
      out - the stream to write to
      Returns:
      a writer that writes to out

    • of

      public static CharWriter of(Appendable out)
      Returns a writer that writes to an Appendable, such as a StringBuilder, which it then owns: it flushes it if it is Flushable, and closes it if it is Closeable. Each write goes to it directly, unless it is a Writer. If out is the stream view of a writer, returns that writer.
      Parameters:
      out - where to write
      Returns:
      a writer that writes to out

    • asWriter

      public Writer asWriter()
      Returns a stream that writes through this writer, for APIs that take a Writer. Writes on the stream and on this writer go through the same buffer, in the order they are made. Closing the stream closes this writer.
      Returns:
      a stream that writes through this writer

    • close

      public void close() throws IOException
      Writes the buffered characters to the stream, then closes it if it is Closeable, even if writing fails, or flushes it if it is only Flushable. Closing a writer again has no effect.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface Closeable
      Throws:
      IOException - if the stream cannot be written or closed; if both fail, the second exception is suppressed by the first
